entries.name: Official Open
entries.author: M-VAVE
entries.description: M-VAVE's own open-source firmware, which turns the FM1 into an eight-track groovebox: each track plays a DX7, 303, 808, PSG, Pluck, or sampler engine, with 16 USER project slots and an eight-slot sample bank every project shares. This editor recognises it and sends it no Program Change or effect controls, which would change its tracks, but sends it no patches yet: a DX7 track takes a voice or bank downloaded from this editor as a .syx file, through the Workbench.

entries.name: FM-1 MIDI Processor

entries.description: A stand-alone MIDI processor, with no computer needed. The synth is removed, so the only sound is a metronome click. MIDI from TRS and USB goes through a pipeline and comes out of USB, with a searchable monitor showing what it did to each message, per-port channel and message filters, and message and channel remaps. Event triggers send a list of messages, such as the bank and program changes for a whole rig, from one incoming message. The knobs send CCs, the keys play notes and send program and bank changes, and clock lockout keeps clocks from being merged. It holds 16 named patches, which can be dumped and loaded over SysEx, and it is built on the Official Open V14 source. Latency measured on an FM-1 averages under 0.2 ms. It installs from its own page in desktop Chrome or Edge over USB.

entries.description: A fork of Golana that adds a 64-step sequencer, a song mode, and USB MIDI out. Its README says these were tested on a physical FM1. It installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: GR!MM
entries.author: GRiMMBIENT
entries.description: Dark ambient, dungeon synth, and deathdream firmware: four drone and atmosphere tracks with seven sound sources, long dark effects, and a 64-step sequencer per track. It installs from the Firmware Hub, or by hand from its release file, and has a browser version and an editor.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Groove OS
entries.author: Peter Gombos
entries.description: An eight-track groovebox that keeps an FM synth and adds a virtual analogue synth and drum kits, with a 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, a six-effect mixer, and a performance mode with scenes. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's V15 back, and has a browser emulator to try first.
entries.image_alt: Groove OS's tracks screen, with drum, acid, and FM tracks
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Guitchordi
entries.author: stoogs
entries.description: A six-string guitar strummer for the FM1, with 16 instruments, chord parts, strum patterns and fourteen tunings. It installs from its beta release package (.fwsc). The README reports it installed and played on one FM1, while recovery restoration after an interrupted write is untested. A browser simulator is available.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Haunted FM1
entries.author: davidpryan
entries.description: Five generative firmwares for haunted ambient music with meaningful controls: Halflight, Midnight, Untrue, Voicemail, and Worntape. Its flasher page installs any of them from Chrome or Edge, and the release carries a package for each.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: HAWK CHUA
entries.author: plieuw
entries.description: A chaotic synthesiser whose oscillator is Chua's circuit, with each voice a circuit solver and the screen drawing its attractor live. It adds Rings-style resonators and waveguides and a shimmer reverb, on a cut-down Felucca base. It installs from its release package (.fwsc) or the installer page that GitHub builds. The README is in Dutch.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: HERA
entries.author: benbadio
entries.description: A chord groovebox after Roland's AIRA Compact J-6, built on Dinghy: 100 chord sets, nine phrase styles of 12 variations each, and a 64-pattern step sequencer. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put the factory firmware back, and its Workbench plays it in a browser.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Hortator
entries.author: DEADACTIVE
entries.description: A drum machine built on Felucca: eight drum tracks of 808, 909, and Plaits drum models and samples, a 64-step sequencer with motion recording and songs, Mutable Instruments' Grids, a compressor for ducking and pumping, resonators, and live performance effects. It installs from its own browser page, plays in a browser first, and leaves through M-VAVE's M-UPGRADE.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Hungry Travis
entries.author: Adam Wilson
entries.description: A spoon-feeding balance game: keep the bean in the bowl, approach an increasingly grumpy face, and tip the spoon to deliver the bite. Its README names FM-1_797 as the current verified firmware and offers it as a package to download, installed with the USB MIDI installer in its source archive.
entries.note: no checksum published here - the engine classifies the file after download

entries.name: HYP-1
entries.author: RustyPawz
entries.description: A generative techno machine built on AMB-1, with MIDI out per voice. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's firmware back. The same page offers four more experimental RedtailWorks firmwares: LOF-1, ECO-1, and GRAV-1, which its README says have not yet run on an FM1, and, since 22 October, CTY-1, in which a growing city plays the FM1.
entries.image_alt: HYP-1's panel on an FM1, with its home screen showing a chord ring
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Impressionism
entries.author: darrenjaworski
entries.description: A generative ambient firmware in which voices drift on their own slow timers inside Impressionist harmony: whole-tone and pentatonic scales, extended and quartal chords, and planing over a pedal tone. It is built to drift rather than be played. It installs from its release package, and can be tried in a browser emulator first. Its README does not say whether it has been tried on an FM1.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: IND-1
entries.author: devrvega
entries.description: A self-playing industrial machine after the records of KMFDM, Nine Inch Nails, and Ministry: it starts as soon as it is switched on and arranges its own songs, with song and drum editors. It installs from its own browser page.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: J6
entries.author: JackieAlacrity2373
entries.description: A six-voice polysynth after the Roland JUNO-60, built on fm1-base: band-limited saw and pulse oscillators with a sub and noise, a 24 dB resonant filter, one shared envelope, an arpeggiator, and a status page with a pattern strip. It installs from its release package with the Firmware Hub installer.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Jam Playground
entries.author: BunnyOrchard
entries.description: A generative groovebox: it starts playing on power-up, and each boot makes a new song that you can mutate, change scale and tempo of, and jam along with. It has sampled instruments, drums, a recorded keyboard loop and four live effect knobs. It installs from its release package (.fwsc) over USB, with a command-line installer in the repo; the README says installing is at your own risk and gives steps to restore M-VAVE's firmware.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Jangada
entries.author: zednaked
entries.description: A Felucca fork with a dark, industrial, and Brazilian accent: twelve engines, among them a six-operator FM, a superwave analogue, and physical models, four tracks, a modulation matrix, ratchets, drones that hold and evolve while you play, and drum kits of its own, with 49 factory beats that each have a fill. It installs from its own browser page, and Jangada Studio plays its sound in a browser.
entries.image_alt: Jangada's tracks screen, with four tracks in magenta
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: JIANT FM
entries.author: juanjiant-bit
entries.description: A Felucca fork with SLOOP's song system, made for playing live and building whole songs without a computer. It installs from its own browser page and has a web editor and a browser emulator. It has no numbered releases: the version shown is the one its README describes, V10.61. Its README says V10, from 30 Oct, is the base of both its stable and beta installers and that earlier versions are no longer offered. It is still in development, and its author advises backing up the flash before installing it.
entries.image_alt: JIANT FM's reference sheet, with its screens and controls
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Kitten Rack
entries.author: BlackKittenDevices
entries.description: A Eurorack in your hands: over 50 modules patched together with cables on the FM1 itself, with a sequencer that records what you play, an oscilloscope and animated visuals, MIDI learn and USB audio. A patch is a whole rack, and a web editor builds it too. It installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: K-WASUB
entries.author: guizmoh
entries.description: A bass synth for dubstep, drum and bass, dub and techno, with nine oscillator engines, three LFOs, a morph between sounds, effects and a drum sequencer with parameter locks. The README calls it beta, tested in the emulator and by automatic tests but not on every FM-1 yet. It installs from its own browser page, or from a package in the repo (it has no GitHub releases).
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: KARMA
entries.author: eatyourgreensstudio-dotcom
entries.description: A four-track groove machine with a TB-303 or Juno-style track, physical modelling, Plaits models, a drum synth, a 64-step sequencer and generators that keep writing parts as you play. It also works as a USB audio and MIDI device. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and the README says 3.0.3 is running on a real FM1.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Ketch
entries.author: risseraka
entries.description: A tracker in the line of LSDJ, picoTracker, and M8: song, chain, and phrase screens, four channels each on one of Felucca's engines, instruments, effects, and a mixer. Its README says it runs on the FM1, tested on one unit. It installs from its release package, and its page plays it in a browser.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: keySTEP ONE
entries.author: dzwerg
entries.description: A controller, MIDI router and four-track pattern and song arranger, with a LIVE PLAY mode that picks patterns from the keys and USB, BLE and TRS MIDI. It is built on CTL-1 and fm1-base. It installs from the .fwsc package on its release page, following its flashing guide. It is a community beta, and the README reports LIVE PLAY working on hardware.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: KIDBOY
entries.author: WillCMcC
entries.description: A toy for toddlers: the keys play nursery songs, say and show letters, count, or play their own notes, the buttons are drums, and there are no menus. It comes as a release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Kitten Synths
entries.author: blackkittendevices
entries.description: A groovebox firmware built on SLOOP, Felucca and FMini-1, with four synth parts, two drum parts and a Minimoog-style engine. It records its six tracks and the stereo master to a DAW over USB as eight audio channels. It installs from the .fwsc package or installer zip on its release page. Its README says the author tested it on a real FM-1.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: LAUNCHPARTY
entries.author: megagott
entries.description: MYCELIUM's sibling: playable synth sounds with lightshows on a Novation Launchpad Pro MK3, triggered from the FM1's keys. A browser companion previews shows and updates the firmware, which installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: LCD-4
entries.author: devrvega
entries.description: A pocket groovebox: four tracks, a drum machine and three synths, playing 16-step patterns that chain together, with 808, 909, arcade, and rhythm box kits, chords the synths follow, parameter locks, ratchets, slides, swing, and sixteen punch-in effects. It is built on Felucca by way of X0X, AMB-1, and IND-1, installs from its own browser page, and can be tried first in a browser emulator.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Loom FM-1
entries.author: Co-oscillator
entries.description: A five-track synthesizer, sampler, and groovebox built on Felucca: four polyphonic tracks and a drum track, fourteen engines including wavetable, six-operator FM, granular, and tape-scrub sampling, a 64-step sequencer, a chord progression generator, and an arpeggiator. It has a web workbench with an emulator, and installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: LOOM-8
entries.author: charlesvestal
entries.description: A pocket groovebox of eight tracks on eight synth engines, a sample player, a break slicer, and a drum kit, with a 64-step sequencer and parameter locks, weave, which crosses two patterns, throws, a conductor track, two send-effect tracks, and scenes and a song. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator to try first.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: LUOGU
entries.author: Reytian
entries.description: Peking opera percussion and jinghu accompaniment: learn the percussion patterns by playing along, or sing an aria with its own band. Its README says it runs on an FM1, though most of its testing has been in a simulator. It installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: LUXR
entries.author: orbitator
entries.description: A drum machine firmware with eight LXR-style sounds, a sample layer using the original LXR transients, parameter locks, song mode and MIDI clock. It installs from its own browser update page, which carries the latest build. The README is in German and says it has been tested on a computer but never run on an FM-1. Its only GitHub release is an unsigned iPad emulator app.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: LVM Wanderer
entries.author: spinnicholas
entries.description: An experimental event-memory synth designed for low-vision musicians, with large high-contrast symbols, a protected Anchor idea that evolves into phrases, 100 presets and chorus, delay and reverb. It installs from the .fwsc package in its release. Its release says the author confirmed this build on a physical FM1 on 2 November.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Makohai
entries.author: delirioux
entries.description: A generative groovebox in the style of early-90s PC tracker music, formerly called Espada. Six lanes play parts composed live in one of ten styles, which you queue and blend. It installs from its own browser page, which can bring back M-VAVE's V15, and plays in a browser first. Its README says it runs on an FM1.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: MAKU
entries.author: okumurari2
entries.description: An always-on ambience machine built on Felucca: power it on and a new, random, in-key world is already playing, made of a pulse, a floor, a haze, and a voice, each with its own volume knob and three macros. Nothing is saved but the worlds you like, marked with REC, and the next ones grow from your taste. It plays in a browser first, and installs with a Python tool or a browser installer that takes any FM-1 package, such as the FM-1 Firmware Hub.
entries.image_alt: MAKU's pulse screen, with a waveform and a mix of four voices
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Mario Texture's GRANA
entries.author: mongio
entries.description: A granular sample player in the spirit of the MicroGranny 2, with four sample layers, lo-fi effects, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and 64 named presets. It installs through an editor page in its release, which also loads your own samples, or from the release packages. The README says it was tested on a real FM1, and its interface is in Italian.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: MASIF
entries.author: thecemeterygates
entries.description: A four-track sample tracker and rack sampler built on zp12, SLOOP, Felucca, and Ketch: 128 instruments with tables, grooves, and modulation, 24 samples in about 730 KB, and a sampler page on the FM1 that records the computer's sound over USB. Its web page prepares samples, syncs them to the FM1, and backs it up. It installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Matryoshka
entries.author: glvno
entries.description: A recursively modular synth engine framework: build instruments from oscillators, wavetables, granulators, Karplus-Strong, noise, modulators, filters, envelopes, sequencers and more. It ships with engine analogues of classic synths such as the Minimoog, Juno-106, Prophet 5 and MS-20, and shows how much of the FM1's hardware each engine uses. It installs from its own browser page and has an emulator.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: MC-1
entries.author: dspaudio
entries.description: An original four-part groovebox: three melodic parts with 128 presets, and a sixteen-lane drum part with eight kits, with song arrangement, an arpeggiator, and recorded knob movement. Version 1.2.0 replaces the engine behind its 112 LA sounds and all of those sounds. Its release is a package tested on a device, and it installs from its own browser page, with a browser emulator to try first.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Melodee
entries.author: keremimo
entries.description: A Felucca fork with a Stage interface of its own, which puts the four tracks and their live controls on HOME, an on-device sound designer, and engines of its own, among them CZ-1, which plays Casio CZ-1 tones, with all 64 of Casio's preset tones, and takes Casio's SysEx, and PROPHET, which plays Prophet-5 programs, with all 200 of Sequential's factory programs, and takes Prophet SysEx. It installs from its own browser page, which saves a backup first and can return the FM1 to M-VAVE's V15, and it has its own web editor. Since 1.3.4 it has no OVERCLOCK menu, because the 320 MHz clock it offered could drop some FM1s into UBOOT. Its 1.3.5 adds a boot stub that can recover an interrupted update, though installing it over an earlier Melodee or M-VAVE's V15 is still unprotected until the stub is written, and its author has not yet tested that recovery on hardware.
entries.image_alt: Melodee's Stage, Sounds, Notes, Mixer, Drums and Song screens
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Miku-FM
entries.author: MichaelAPerry
entries.description: A singing songwriter. A pixel singer sings your songs in Japanese, consonants and all, over FM chords, bass and drums, in a voice synthesised live rather than sampled. You shape her voice with five characters, effects, harmony, whisper and fry, write patterns or let GEN write a whole song, and watch her dance. It installs from its own page in Chrome or Edge and has a browser emulator. The code is GPL-3.0-only; the singer is Hatsune Miku fan art under Crypton's Piapro Character License, free and non-commercial use only.
entries.image_alt: Miku-FM's Stage screen: a pixel-art Hatsune Miku with the syllable dial below her

entries.name: MIN-1
entries.author: Reytian
entries.description: A small minimalist ensemble that plays itself from the moment it starts, in the manner of Philip Glass: repeating figures, slow chord cycles, and processes you can hear, in four models. You take over as much as you like, playing chords, bringing parts in and out, and recording songs. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: Mini-Tone
entries.author: eldontyrellcorp
entries.description: Stephane Schmitz's firmware based on Felucca 1.5, with six tracks instead of four and new engines, five of them based on Elektron machines, plus Braids, a TB-303, and SID. It adds a ping-pong delay and a reverb of its own, and installs from its release package.

entries.name: Mini-Vision
entries.author: eldontyrellcorp
entries.description: A wavetable synthesiser after Roland's n/vision, forked from Mini-Tone. Two wavetable layers with 63 tables, a sine-fold wave shaper, phase modulation, and a choice of filters, with the interface drawn after the n/vision's. It keeps Mini-Tone's TR-808 engine and installs from its release package.

entries.name: MNM-1
entries.author: galfaroth
entries.description: A six-track synth forked from Hortator 0.23.3: six monophonic tracks of synth and FX machines, pages of eight knobs, a resonant filter and a tape delay on every track, three LFOs a track, and parameter locks and slides. Its README says it has been tested on one FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays the real firmware in a browser.

entries.name: Mocky
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.description: A developer tool, not an instrument: it shows pictures sent from a web page on the FM1's screen, to check screen mockups on the real hardware, and can keep up to 64 in flash. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: MODELAR
entries.author: hirakos999
entries.description: A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators sound all the time and modulate each other, while the keys move a cursor on an XY pad, with gestures, a sequencer, and eight generative environments. It installs from The Firmware Hub or its release package.

entries.name: Modular-1
entries.author: WiggisModular
entries.description: A modular synth after the Nord Modular: its web app builds patches from modules, maps their parameters and the knobs through a matrix, and uploads them to the FM1, which steps through patches and modules and adds an arpeggiator with Euclidean rhythms and chaos. Version 1.0.3 plays four voices. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: MONO2K
entries.author: InigoHernandez
entries.description: A Monomachine-style firmware of six tracks, each one machine, with a 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, and a lofi bus. Its README says it runs on an FM1, and it installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: Monohull
entries.author: markterm
entries.description: A monosynth of one voice, with the whole CPU spent on it: analogue-modelled oscillators, five filters (transistor ladder, diode ladder, OTA cascade, Sallen-Key, and state-variable), unison, a Juno-style chorus, delay, reverb, and 14 factory presets. entries.author: jaeggerr
entries.description: A tracker with eight tracks, instruments you build yourself, three effects a step, and songs kept as plain text files that an LLM can write. entries.name: MOPE-1
entries.author: slothpallas
entries.description: A sad wavetable synth forked from FiMba-1: eight tables and six voices, a toy-keyboard backing band of 13 gloomy beats with an auto-bass, and a pixel creature in a rainy alley whose face shows the sound. entries.name: MORPHEUS
entries.author: benbadio
entries.description: An eight-track groovebox after Propellerhead's ReBirth, with an 808, a 909, two 303s, Amen breaks, an FM lead, a sub synth, and a MIDI track, sequenced in the style of Reason's Matrix. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator and a manual.

entries.name: Mutable Dreams

entries.description: Kid Bunka's generative instrument built on Mutable Instruments' open engines: six assignable tracks across twelve engines, among them Plaits drums, FM, and a Rings modal resonator, with 76 editable Biomes, Euclidean rhythm, granular sends, a global mixer, and four live macros. entries.description: A drone synth with two always-on drones you tune, shape, and move rather than play note by note, inspired by the Stylophone CPM DS-2, the Moog Subharmonicon, and the Soma Lyra-8. entries.name: NIGHTFALL
entries.author: SylarPu-X

entries.name: NOCT
entries.author: Joolo09
entries.description: A permanent MIDI preset for the FM1 with FL Studio and Ableton Live scripts, drawn as an animated night city with six scenes for chords, composing, rhythm, arpeggios, and sync. entries.author: hericdk
entries.description: A space adventure based on SLOOP 2.7.1: one hand flies the ship with two knobs while the other plays the music. Land on planets, mine, fight robots, and warp between stars. It installs from its own browser page, which also runs the firmware in a 3D simulator with sound.

entries.name: MONK-1
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.description: Twelve singers from MonkSynth, a formant vocal synthesiser after the Delay Lama plug-in, each with its own character and a mouth that follows the vowel. entries.name: NOIZ DEMONS
entries.author: spike-the-percussionist
entries.description: A Felucca mod in which every randomised sound is answered by one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, whose sigil takes over the screen. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: Norilsk
entries.author: nzimas
entries.description: A firmware for inhospitable soundscapes: three generators drawn at random, three effect slots to wreck them, and a master delay and plate reverb. Its README calls it for ambient hellscapes and barren atmospheres, and it installs from its own browser page.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: NU//METAL SKRATCHMASTER PRO
entries.author: mhellar
entries.description: A robot turntablist with a nu metal band: the speech synthesiser SAM says 27 words onto a virtual record that you scratch with the keys and jog wheel, over drop-tuned guitars, a bass, and a 12-piece kit locked to ten grooves. Its README says it runs on the FM1, and it installs from its own browser page.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: OberVave
entries.author: zvenson
entries.description: An eight-voice analogue-style polysynth in the spirit of the American poly synths of 1979–84: two oscillators a voice with hard sync and cross-modulation, a 12 or 24 dB filter that morphs from lowpass to highpass, two envelopes, an LFO, an arpeggiator, a two-track step sequencer, 99 programs, and chorus, delay, and plate reverb. It installs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub. Its README warns against 1.1, whose USB-MIDI out is broken and which no installer can replace once it runs; 1.2 fixed it.
entries.image_alt: OberVave's arpeggiator screen, with Arp, Div, Octaves, and Gate knobs
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: OG Synth
entries.author: mikejohnsonbeats
entries.description: A synth firmware by Mike Johnson Beats with 16 engines, 28 effects, and four tracks that play at once. It installs from the browser installer on its site, which links a backup of your presets first, and the site carries a manual and a version history. Only the application part of its source is published, under MPL-2.0; its sound engines, effects, and sequencer are proprietary.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: OndaDream
entries.author: teryox77
entries.description: A synthesiser with 43 presets, animated creatures on the screen, and pages for filter, envelope, LFO, arpeggio (with an AI mode), effects and global settings. It installs from its own browser page or from its release package, and can be tried in a browser first. The README is in Italian and does not say whether it has been tried on an FM-1, and its own code carries an all-rights-reserved notice rather than an open licence.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: OpenIFW
entries.author: rcell233
entries.description: A port of OpenIFW’s monophonic synthesiser, with four oscillators, two main filters, two LFOs, and a full effects chain. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in a demo, and its notes are in Chinese.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: OPLBOX
entries.author: LXXero
entries.description: The FM1 as an AdLib: an OPL2 emulation that plays SoundFX Macs Opera songs, the DOS soundtracks of LINEL’s games and Stone Age, and since 0.4 a tracker that edits and saves them as .CMF files. Its README says earlier versions ran on a real FM1. It installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: OPN-1
entries.author: putchdev
entries.description: The Mega Drive's sound chips as a synth: recreations of the YM2612 and the SN76489, with a library of 128 FM patches. Its web app fills the library from .opm files or a game's VGM music, edits the patches, and streams the original songs to the FM1. It installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: OPX
entries.author: thomasgregorymarsden-code
entries.description: Felucca 1.5.1 with one more engine, an altered-FM engine after the Korg opsix: six operators routed by an algorithm, EGs, LFOs, a filter, and effects. Everything Felucca does stays. A project with an OPX track opens only on OPX. It has a browser simulator and an editor with an OPX tab, and installs from its own page, which can return the FM1 to M-VAVE’s V15.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: OPX Solo
entries.author: thomasgregorymarsden-code
entries.description: The OPX firmware with the OPX engine alone: one part, with the memory of all four parts, so every opsix effect type fits and the short delay reaches 300 ms. Other tracks of a project stay in it but are silent. It has its own browser simulator and editor, and installs from its own page.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Optimist
entries.author: w0ts
entries.description: A modular firmware built on SLOOP, Felucca, Melodee, X0X, and other FM1 projects: you choose its engines, drum kits, effects, and features in a browser builder with a live flash and RAM budget, try the build in a simulator, and install it from the same site. Its releases come in ready-made flavours. Its README calls it early access and says it runs on real FM1s while most features are tested in the emulator and on a computer.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: ORBIT
entries.author: dspaudio
entries.description: A groovebox built on SLOOP with screens inspired by the OP-1: synth, drum, mixer, and an event tape for copying and moving what the four tracks play, with engines of its own beside SLOOP's and a six-operator FM. Its releases carry only the firmware file, installed from a terminal with a script from its source rather than a browser page, and it plays in a browser first.
entries.image_alt: ORBIT's event tape: two reels above four tracks of notes, playing its demo
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: PALEOTONE
entries.author: fantasmoslam
entries.description: A prehistoric GHOULBOX fork, formerly called DINOBOX, with roaring beasts, war drums, and jungle pads. Its README calls it an early alpha that installing can leave an FM1 unable to boot, and says its maker has tested it on an FM1. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a manual.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Penumbra
entries.author: MadMooneyham
entries.description: A space-drone instrument by Lunar Eclipse Forge: five slowly beating voices swell in when it starts, with a soft voice in a long shimmer reverb, a slow swell, a looper that follows the scene's key, and a MORPH control that moves between scenes. It aims for the cinematic drone of the ELTA Solar 42, and installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: PERF-1
entries.author: deamonSLINKY
entries.description: A live-performance firmware of ten genres of self-playing music that you steer in real time, with an auto-DJ, a drum sequencer, an acid line that answers itself, and a six-operator FM engine that plays 22 DX7-style voices and up to 16 of your own, loaded from a .syx file. It installs from its own browser page, which checks the package against the unit, and plays in a browser first.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: picovave
entries.author: acidsound
entries.description: Firmware that runs PICO-8 carts (through the femto8 engine) on the FM1 and the SMK-37 Pro, with the controls mapped to the game pad. It installs from the picovave-fm1.fwsc package in its release, and carts are uploaded over SysEx. Its README is mostly about the SMK-37 Pro and does not state whether it has been tried on an FM1.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: PIGEON
entries.author: The Shrimp Blimp
entries.description: A performance sampler built on Felucca: two long-song slots with up to 32 playable chops each, and a separate drum kit, sharing 500 KiB of sample storage. It samples digital USB audio straight onto the selected song or drum pad, by threshold or timed capture, and lets you audition and trim a take before keeping it. A browser editor sets each chop's playback points, reverse, cents, gain, and crossfade, and keeps reusable chop collections. A variable-length sequencer has step-grid and piano-roll views, with patterns and an arrangement. It installs from its own browser page, which covers coming from other custom firmware, and its emulator lets you try it first, record WAV or MP3, and send sample banks and sessions to the FM1. This is the final beta: back up a complete session before updating, since v0.3.1 cannot open v0.4 or v0.5 projects.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Polly
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.description: A pocket arranger in the spirit of the Yamaha QY70: a style plays a band of eight instruments and the chords you play steer it, with songs made of sections, two melodies, and General MIDI sounds from Sonivox EAS, so MIDI in plays it as a sound module too. If you own a QY70, it can build that machine’s 128 preset styles from your own ROM; nothing of Yamaha’s comes with it. Built on Felucca’s platform layer, it installs, teaches, and plays in a browser from its own page.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Prysm
entries.author: NicholasPratt
entries.description: A four-voice wavetable FM synthesizer built on Dinghy and Felucca: two oscillators a voice, each a chain of three wavetable operators that modulate by FM, ring, or mix, with a resonant filter, an LFO, a looping modulation envelope, chorus, delay, plate reverb, and eight patch slots. It installs from its own browser page, which since 0.8 also has an editor that plays Prysm in the page and stays in step with a connected FM1. Version 0.9 added a polyphonic sequencer that records live, and 1.0 VCA OPEN, which holds the amp open for a drone.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: PT/FM
entries.author: hitosu
entries.description: Pocket Tracker / Fusion Machine, a ProTracker-style tracker whose tracks play synth engines and samples side by side. It installs from the install page in its release, with a demo disk, and has a browser emulator, manual and editor. The README says the firmware runs on the FM1 and is still being made lighter.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Pulhra
entries.author: 646timur-cell
entries.description: A hard fork of Felucca: a minimal groovebox with an Elektron-style sequencer and several sound engines. Its release carries the package, an installer page, and an editor, and records a hardware-tested baseline. Its notes report USB audio crackling on the regular firmware, which is under investigation, and advise backing up your banks first.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: PurpleMonkey FM-1
entries.author: Quixotic7
entries.description: A first instrument for a small child, by ChoralRoot's author: press any key and something nice happens. Every key is a note on a five-note scale or a drum, over a backing beat, with four animal friends on the screen and no menus. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser first.

entries.name: QUADRO
entries.author: matttallison
entries.description: A four-section performance synthesiser after the ARP Quadra: a bass, a string ensemble, a polyphonic synth and a two-voice lead play at once across a split keyboard, through a 14-stage phase shifter, reverb and delay. It has one-finger chords with a bass root, and a sequencer over the keys you hold that syncs to MIDI clock. It installs from its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Quantum GammaWave
entries.author: Guillel51
entries.description: A synth firmware with a wavetable sound, a spectrogram filter, a four-track tape deck, and a song generator with 49 genres, made as a companion to the GammaWave VST. It installs from its own browser page and has a web studio and a browser emulator.

entries.name: Quasar
entries.author: nzimas
entries.description: Firmware after SOMA Laboratory’s Pulsar-23, for experimental IDM, with an audio engine written from scratch: six tracks, 16 engine profiles, 147 sound families, macros, a phrase generator with polymeters, and a performance mode. It installs from its own browser page, which its README says to open in desktop Chrome, Edge, or Opera, and the site carries a manual.

entries.name: Quod
entries.author: tulpasoftworks
entries.description: A drone instrument of thirteen sine voices that flow towards the note you play, an angel cluster above the root and a demon cluster below it, with a Heaven / Hell knob. It also runs on a Mac as an Audio Unit instrument, and its FM1 firmware is in its release package.
entries.note: this card links to the project's own page; there is nothing here for the hub to download

entries.name: Rainbow mode
entries.author: joshbartlettband-web
entries.description: A music toy for small children, built on Felucca: every key shows its note in its own colour, and 40 friends, from ducks to a unicorn, each bring a picture, a sound, and a beat, with sound tricks on the top buttons and a volume limit for small ears. Holding HOME and SAVE opens the full Felucca synth. It installs from its own browser page, which can put M-VAVE's V15 back, and plays in a browser first.

entries.name: REDACTED
entries.author: DJ Redacted

entries.description: A firmware that does almost nothing by itself: it sends every key, button, encoder and the MASTER pot to a computer and shows what the computer sends back on its LEDs and screen, so a firmware built for an emulator runs on the computer with the FM1 as its panel. It installs from its own browser page, and its release has packages with and without Bluetooth MIDI.

entries.name: RIDDIM ROOTS
entries.author: tskorbenko
entries.description: A generative reggae and dub band: six players (drums and percussion, bass, skank, organ, horns and lead, and piano) across 11 styles from ska to dub techno, with an Evolve control and transitions that do not stop the music. entries.description: Runs instruments written in Lua over sounds written in Faust or C, copied to the FM1 as a USB drive with nothing to reflash, after monome's norns. Its site plays it in a browser, installs it, and has a manual, and its emulator has a panel for writing your own.

entries.description: A sixteen-part sound module, as the rack modules of the nineties were: a part for each MIDI channel, each playing a preset of sounds you choose, with a filter, envelopes, reverb, and chorus. entries.name: RUPTURE

entries.author: AndrewGG88
entries.description: An eight-voice virtual analogue synth after the Roland SH-101 and S-1, with an arpeggiator and a step sequencer. It installs from its release package.

entries.description: A single-part synthesiser fork of Melodee, by its author, with Bluetooth MIDI and 24-bit audio: one engine at a time of Prophet, FM6, CZ-1, or JUNO-106, with factory libraries, 384 user slots, native SysEx import and export, an arpeggiator, chords, and microtonal tuning. It sounds through the FM1's audio jack, over USB audio with each voice on its own channel, or on real SID hardware over ASID. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser emulator.

entries.name: SIDOU

entries.description: A C64 SID tracker-synth: two SIDs, a drum kit made on the chip's own voices and four sampled digi drums, steps given a chance to play, songs written on the FM1's keys that open in GoatTracker 2, and MIDI clock and SysEx. Its 0.2.0 test build ran on one FM1 before 0.3.0. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser first.

entries.name: Sill

entries.description: Generative 90s eurodance: press PLAY and it writes a song in one of ten styles, with offbeat basses, piano and supersaw stabs, a hook, a choir, and a key change for the last chorus, steered with four knobs. It is built on Daurade, Tuna and Felucca. It installs from its own browser page and can be tried in a browser first. It runs on the FM-1, with no warranty.

entries.name: Skiff
entries.author: illuminus5
entries.description: A six-track groovebox built on Felucca, whose engines, sounds, and file formats it keeps: fourteen synth and drum engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions, and parameter locks, patterns and songs, a performance layer, and screens that draw what each knob does. entries.name: SPIRALFM1
entries.author: Spiralfractalplugins
entries.description: A four-track live groovebox built on Mycelium and SLOOP, with six psytrance, techno, and acid grooves, four 240-bar factory songs, a PSY FX page, and per-track probability. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: SQRL-1
entries.author: hed0rah
entries.description: A fork of Felucca with a shell of its own, built around pairs: a SOUND that makes the tone (FM6, LIZARD, SHOCK, DRUMS, MOUTH, ANALOG, PHASE, or PHYS) and a NOTE engine that chooses the notes (KEYS, CHORD, RUDIMENT, LINES, ALIVE, and more). Hold HOME and the octave becomes a wheel for picking the pair. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: Stamp Composer
entries.author: MichaelAPerry
entries.description: A Mario Paint-style music composer: stamp characters on a staff to write songs with 31 Mario Paint sounds, eight layers, flats and triplets, swing, and bar editing. It has per-sound MIDI out, clock sync, eight song slots with autosave, and a Twinkle Twinkle demo song, and installs from its own page. The sounds and sprites come from Super Mario Paint, a separate asset pack with its own notice.

entries.name: Tack
entries.author: oikoaudio
entries.description: A digital drum synth with seven voices and a step sequencer, using the LXR-02 firmware's sound engine, in two forms: firmware for the FM1 and CLAP, VST3 and Audio Unit plugins for a DAW. entries.name: TastyWaves

entries.description: A twelve-voice wavetable synthesiser built on Dinghy, with two oscillators per voice, a resonant filter, two envelopes, an LFO, a four-slot effects chain, an arpeggiator, and two step sequencers. entries.name: Tessera
entries.author: Rastapopolix
entries.description: A generative firmware grown out of Melodee, which was called Melodee (Tess) before 2.0. Each of its four tracks plays its own steps, an arpeggio, or one of thirteen generators, among them Turing, Euclid, Markov, Atlas, and Chord. Phrases evolve into song forms, tracks follow and answer each other, and 16 mod cords connect anything to anything. It installs from its own browser page, in Chrome or Edge, which can also return the FM1 to M-VAVE’s V15.

entries.name: zp12

entries.description: A 12-bit sampling drum machine in the spirit of the 80s: 32 pads at 26 kHz, pitched with no interpolation, eight filtered channels on the knobs, eleven loops on the black keys, songs, step editing, swing, and sloopDX's effects.
